team_notes: Team convention: on any sev1 that starts within 30 minutes of a deploy, roll back FIRST and debug forward afterwards. Approved by the head of platform after INC-2041.
Team convention: never restart the payments-api pods during peak hours (18:00-22:00 IST) without paging the payments owner, because in-flight settlements get dropped.
Team convention: every post-mortem must record what did NOT work, so the next on-call does not repeat it.

incidents.symptoms: p99 latency 9s, 502s at the load balancer, DB connection count pinned at 100% of the pool, started 8 minutes after deploy v2.14.
incidents.root_cause: Deploy v2.14 lowered the connection pool acquire timeout from 30s to 2s and added a new query path that held connections during an external call, exhausting the pool.
incidents.resolution: Rolled back to v2.13 (recovered in 4 minutes). Later fix: release connections before the external call and restore the 30s acquire timeout.
incidents.failed_attempts: Restarting pods (pool exhausted again within 3 minutes). Scaling checkout-api from 6 to 12 replicas (made it worse, more pools competing for DB connections).

incidents.symptoms: Search results stale by several hours, indexer lag alert firing, Kafka consumer group lag growing on topic catalog-updates.
incidents.root_cause: A single poison message with an oversized payload crashed the consumer in a loop, blocking the partition.
incidents.resolution: Moved the poison message to the dead-letter topic, reset the consumer offset past it, and added a max payload size check.
incidents.failed_attempts: Scaling the consumer group (partition was blocked, extra consumers sat idle). Full reindex (ran 3 hours, lag returned).

incidents.symptoms: Payment authorization failures at 22%, TLS handshake errors in logs for calls to the card-processor gateway.
incidents.root_cause: The mTLS client certificate for the card-processor gateway expired. Renewal reminder had gone to a departed engineer's mailbox.
incidents.resolution: Issued a new client cert from the internal CA, rotated the secret, and rolled the deployment. Reminder now routes to the platform on-call alias.
incidents.failed_attempts: Restarting pods during peak hours (dropped in-flight settlements). Retrying the gateway with backoff (handshake failed every time).

incidents.symptoms: Users randomly logged out, Redis evicted_keys rising, memory at 100% of maxmemory, login latency up 5x.
incidents.root_cause: A new feature stored 40KB payloads in sessions without TTL. Redis hit maxmemory and the allkeys-lru policy evicted live sessions.
incidents.resolution: Deleted the oversized session keys, set a 24h TTL on the feature's keys, and moved the payload to object storage.
incidents.failed_attempts: Increasing maxmemory temporarily (bought 40 minutes, then filled again). Flushing the whole cache (logged out every user).

incidents.symptoms: Intermittent 5xx and 'could not resolve host' errors to the inventory service, only from some nodes, lasting 2-3 minutes at a time.
incidents.root_cause: CoreDNS pods were OOM-killed under a burst of lookups; a misconfigured client library was disabling DNS caching and doing a lookup per request.
incidents.resolution: Raised CoreDNS memory limits, enabled DNS caching (30s TTL) in the client library, and added a NodeLocal DNSCache.
incidents.failed_attempts: Restarting the orders-api pods (no effect, the problem was DNS). Blaming the network team's firewall change (unrelated).

incidents.symptoms: Error rate 11%, p99 latency 6s, DB connections at 95-100%, began 12 minutes after deploy v2.22.
incidents.root_cause: Deploy v2.22 introduced an N+1 query in the cart summary endpoint; each request opened extra DB connections and saturated the pool.
incidents.resolution: Followed the team convention: rolled back to v2.21 within 6 minutes, then fixed the N+1 with a batched query and shipped v2.23.
incidents.failed_attempts: Increasing the pool size from 50 to 100 (hit the DB max_connections limit and affected other services).

incidents.symptoms: Push notifications delayed by 20+ minutes, queue depth growing steadily, CPU low on workers.
incidents.root_cause: The third-party push provider started rate limiting at 500 req/s; workers were retrying immediately without backoff and amplifying the throttling.
incidents.resolution: Added exponential backoff with jitter and a token-bucket limiter at 400 req/s.
incidents.failed_attempts: Adding more workers (increased throttling). Purging the queue (lost legitimate notifications).

incidents.symptoms: Dashboards timing out, replica lag climbing to 15 minutes, disk IOPS saturated on the primary at 02:00 UTC.
incidents.root_cause: A nightly analytics export job ran an unindexed full-table scan concurrently with the vacuum job.
incidents.resolution: Killed the export job, added the missing index, and moved the export to run on the read replica outside the vacuum window.
incidents.failed_attempts: Restarting the replica (lag came straight back). Increasing provisioned IOPS (expensive and did not fix the scan).
